newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end a tad higher after paring some gains.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end a tad higher after paring some gains.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher after paring some gains toward the close on Thursday.
Traders said a Jiji news agency report which quoted a key business leader as saying a review of Japan's monetary policy may get under way from the summer, pulled JGBs down toward the close.
"Large-lot selling of JGB futures appeared after the comments were reported," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
"It is about time that discussions (over the review of monetary policy) started," Jiro Ushio, chairman of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives, was quoted as saying by Jiji.

"Discussions may get under way from the summer towards the end of the year taking into account the business conditions at smaller firms, the bad loan issue at financial institutions, and the management of financial institutions ahead of the 'Big Bang' (financial reforms)," Ushio was quoted as saying.
The June ended at 126.63, up slightly from the previous day's close of 126.60. Turnover was 49,244 contracts.
Ushio's reported comments were unlikely to lead to a drastic change in the market's view of interest rates, the trust bank trader said.
Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc's launch of 100 billion yen worth of 10-year 2.5 percent straight bonds earlier on Thursday would likely be met with at least moderate investor demand, traders said.

"I don't think they (TEPCO's bonds) will be an instant sell-out, but I don't think we need to worry about the bonds having a negative impact on JGBs," said an analyst at a second-tier brokerage house.
Traders said the market would be watching to see whether the Bank of Japan conducts an outright bond buying operation on Friday.
They said JGBs would likely to fall if the BOJ reduces the amount of its monthly outright bond purchases, but added that the market was not sure at this point what the BOJ was up to.

"Although the BOJ has not conducted an outright bond buying operation so far this week, it is not clear at this point whether the BOJ has actually decided to reduce the amount of its outright bond buying," the first trader said.
The BOJ has conducted two outright bond-buying operations per month and bought 100 billion yen worth of JGBs each time since January.
Its last outright bond-buying operation was on April 11, when it offered to buy 100 billion yen worth of JGBs.
JGBs fell on Wednesday due partly to a vague rumour that the BOJ may reduce the amount of its monthly outright bond purchases.
The Finance Ministry said on Thursday its auction of 120 billion yen worth of 0.7 percent two-year notes produced a lowest price of 99.90 and an average price of 99.93,
